title: The knot's count reads the Euler characteristic: it forces a violated line only on the sphere
claim: Let a signed knot space be read off a two-coloured triangulation of a closed surface S of Euler characteristic chi, so its incidence graph is cellularly embedded in S with faces at the triangulation's vertices. (1) Under every assignment each face's number of agreeing corners has a parity fixed by the signs; the faces where it is even form a set D with |D| = chi (mod 2); every such D occurs, and the signings with a given D form 2^(2 - chi) gauge classes, so signings with no even face exist iff chi is even. (2) Under every assignment, violated lines minus the faces' excess agreements (sum of floor(agree/2)) equals (chi - |D|)/2: the count forces a violated line iff chi > |D|, which happens only on the sphere with Kasteleyn signs, and forces excess at the faces iff chi < |D| (for example on every surface of genus at least 2 with no even face); orientability never enters. (3) When chi = |D| the satisfying assignments are, two to one, the perfect matchings of the lines with the faces outside D whose mod-2 homology class is the one the signs prescribe. (4) On a lattice torus a sign class is satisfiable iff the slope triangle conv{(0,0), (p,q), (0,-r)} contains an integer point of matching parity; the unsatisfiable classes are exactly one on each degenerate torus, one on each thin torus (circumference sqrt 3) of even index, and the untwisted class of the two Fano tori; thin tori are cyclic chains, on which binary search finds a violated line with O(log n) queries. (5) By computation, simple lattice Klein bottles, hexagonal projective planes and genus-2 double covers are satisfiable in every tested sign class.
failure_conditions: A face whose agreeing-corner parity changes with the assignment, or an even-face set of the wrong parity.
A gauge-class count other than 2^(2 - chi), or a set D of the right parity that no signing realizes.
An assignment violating the identity violated lines - sum floor(agree/2) = (chi - |D|)/2.
A corner map accepted by no sign class or by two, or a class whose satisfying assignments are not two per accepted map.
A lattice torus whose satisfiable classes differ from the triangle criterion, or an unsatisfiable class outside the three listed kinds.
A thin torus on which the binary search fails or needs more than O(log n) queries.
A simple lattice Klein bottle, hexagonal projective plane or genus-2 cover with an unsatisfiable tested class.
foundation_claim_scope: Every closed surface and every two-coloured triangulation for (1)-(3); every lattice torus for (4) (by proof, with index <= 21 decided by computation; SAT agreement checked for index <= 40, the criterion's classification for index <= 120); (5) is computational: Klein bottles with m*h <= 64 in both glide families, projective planes of side <= 6, seven tori's genus-2 covers, and double covers of K_2..K_4.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-07.
validation.status: by hand; finite claims checked by computation with controls; no human or external review
validation.novelty: known-with-delta: the parity and class count are the bipartite Kasteleyn condition on surfaces (Kasteleyn 1963; Cimasoni and Reshetikhin 2007; Cimasoni 2009 for non-orientable surfaces); lemma 5.1 is the honeycomb case of the realization of every integer point of the Newton polygon (Kenyon, Okounkov and Sheffield 2006; Ibeas Martin 2012); on lattice tori the satisfying assignments are zero-frustration ground states of the triangular Ising antiferromagnet, and for unbounded genus the related satisfying-state problem is NP-complete (Jimenez and Kiwi 2011). New as far as found: the not-all-equal count's defect identity on surfaces and which side it forces, the matching correspondence for the knot's constraints, the list of unsatisfiable lattice tori, and the orientation-blindness of the count's forcing (PPADS^dt membership on every surface, never PPA^dt-hard).
